title_en: Yang Erte v. Liquan County Education Bureau, Liquan County Education Trade Union — dispute over payment of donation funds
keywords_en: civil; donation dispute; first instance; basic people's court; Shaanxi Province; natural person; state organ; General Principles of Civil Law; ownership of donated funds; donor's right of disposal; principle of good faith; partial support; leukemia; donation; misappropriation of donations; good faith; dispute over payment of donated funds by county education labor union
full_text_en:
Yang Erte v. Liquan County Education Bureau,
Liquan County Education Trade Union
— Dispute over Payment of Donated Funds

Plaintiff: Yang Erte, male, 12 years old, a fifth-grade student at Yangjia Village Primary School, Shitan Township, Liquan County, Shaanxi Province, on medical leave since 1996 due to illness.
Legal Representative: Yang Xucheng, father of Yang Erte.
Agents ad litem: Xu Xiaoping and Li Jie, lawyers of Xu Xiaoping Law Firm, Xi’an.

Defendant: Liquan County Education Bureau, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Cao Xianmin, Director.
Agent ad litem: Wang Jingcheng, official of Liquan County Education Bureau, Shaanxi Province.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Hanying, lawyer of Liquan County Law Firm, Shaanxi Province.

Defendant: China Education Trade Union Liquan County Committee, Shaanxi Province.
Responsible Person: Wang Feng, Vice Chairman.
Agent ad litem: Wang Zhigang, lawyer of Shaanxi No. 4 Law Firm.

Plaintiff Yang Erte filed a lawsuit with the Liquan County People’s Court of Shaanxi Province against defendants Liquan County Education Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Education Bureau) and China Education Trade Union Liquan County Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Education Trade Union) for a dispute over recovery of donated funds.

Plaintiff’s Allegations
The plaintiff alleged that he was diagnosed with leukemia on August 15, 1996. Due to his family’s financial difficulties and inability to afford medical treatment, he sought help from society. At the suggestion of relevant leaders, the defendant Education Bureau and the Education Trade Union issued an initiative in the plaintiff’s name, calling on teachers and students across the county to raise donations for the plaintiff’s medical treatment. A total of RMB 40,733.45 was collected. However, the Education Bureau only gave the plaintiff RMB 10,000 on December 3, 1996, and the remaining RMB 30,733.45 has not been paid to date. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to order the defendants to return the full amount of the donated funds and to compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 4,569.20 and moral damages of RMB 3,000 incurred in pursuing the recovery of the donated funds.

The Two Defendants’ Joint Defense
The defendants jointly responded that the defendant Education Bureau, at the suggestion of relevant leaders, issued an initiative to teachers and students across the county, calling for “warmth and love” and donations for the medical treatment of the plaintiff, Yang Erte. When several thousand yuan in donations were received, reports were also received from the three townships of Junma, Shitan, and Zhaozhen, stating that three other students and one teacher suffering from leukemia also needed assistance and requesting that initiatives be issued for them as well. In light of this situation, the two defendants instructed all schools to strengthen publicity, actively mobilize teachers and students to donate, and required that all donated funds be turned over to the Education Bureau for unified allocation and use. The defendants received a total of RMB 40,482.05 in donations. From this amount, they paid RMB 10,000 to Yang Erte, and also paid RMB 4,000 to Luo Qianqian, a student suffering from the same disease, RMB 7,000 to Kou Peng, RMB 7,000 to Du Ming, and RMB 4,000 to teacher Dong Cheng. The remaining more than RMB 8,000 was deposited in a bank for later disposition. The defendants’ initiative to solicit donations to help others was a just act and not illegal. Yang Erte needed assistance, but the other four teachers and students also needed assistance. The defendants’ allocation of the donated funds to other teachers and students was not open to criticism. The court should not grant the plaintiff’s claim for full return of these funds. The plaintiff’s claims for compensation for economic losses and moral damages arising from the pursuit of the donated funds were even more unfounded in fact and law, and should be dismissed by the court.

Facts Found by the Liquan County People’s Court through Open Trial
On August 15, 1996, the plaintiff, Yang Erte, was diagnosed with leukemia and required hospitalization. Yang Xucheng, Yang Erte’s father, was unable to afford the medical expenses and sought help from society. At the suggestion of relevant county leaders, the defendant Education Bureau and the Education Trade Union jointly issued an initiative on October 22, 1996, calling on teachers and students of all primary and secondary schools in the county to donate money to Yang Erte. Donations totaling RMB 40,482.05 were received from 30 units, and receipts were issued stating “Donation for Yang Erte’s medical treatment.” On December 3, 1996, Yang Xucheng received RMB 10,000 from the Education Bureau. On August 13, 1997, the Education Bureau paid RMB 4,000 to Luo Qianqian, a student suffering from leukemia, RMB 7,000 to Kou Peng, RMB 7,000 to Du Ming, and RMB 4,000 to teacher Dong Cheng. The remaining more than RMB 8,000 was deposited in a bank. Yang Erte’s leukemia still required continued treatment.

The above facts are confirmed by the trial records, statements of the parties, receipts for funds received, disbursement slips, and the initiative, among other evidence, and are sufficient to establish them.

Opinion of the Liquan County People’s Court
The court held that when the plaintiff, Yang Erte, was unable to afford medical treatment for leukemia, the defendants, the Education Bureau and the Education Trade Union, issued an initiative to teachers and students across the county to solicit donations. This was a just act in line with socialist spiritual civilization. The initiative was specifically issued to assist Yang Erte, a specific beneficiary. The receipts issued by the Education Bureau to the 30 donating units also stated that the funds received were “donations for Yang Erte’s medical treatment.” This evidence demonstrated that the funds were donated by the donors for the purpose of treating Yang Erte’s illness. A social donation legal relationship was established among the Education Bureau, the Education Trade Union, the donors, and Yang Erte. The Education Bureau and the Education Trade Union, as solicitors of donations, were entrusted by the donors to manage and supervise these specific donations and had the obligation to deliver the donated funds to the beneficiary for the specific purpose in accordance with the donors’ intent, thereby protecting the lawful rights and interests of both the donors and the beneficiary. Yang Erte was the lawful beneficiary of these donations and was entitled to receive the funds, but also had the obligation to use them in accordance with the donors’ intent. Knowing that Yang Erte’s illness still required continued treatment and that his family’s financial difficulties necessitated further social assistance, the Education Bureau and the Education Trade Union, by taking advantage of their temporary possession of the donations, acted contrary to the donors’ intent by paying only RMB 10,000 of the donated funds to Yang Erte and diverting the remaining RMB 30,482.05 to other uses. This conduct violated the principle of good faith as provided in Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People’s Republic of China and was indeed improper. As for the defendants’ assertion that the donation drive also covered fundraising for the other four teachers and students, the court did not accept this defense. Yang Erte’s request for the two defendants to return the remaining donated funds should be supported. Yang Erte’s other claims were not supported.

Accordingly, on December 23, 1997, the Liquan County People’s Court rendered the following judgment:

1. Within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, the two defendants shall pay the remaining donated funds of RMB 30,482.05 to the plaintiff.
2. The plaintiff’s other claims are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 1,170 and other expenses of RMB 530, totaling RMB 1,700, shall be borne by the two defendants in the amount of RMB 1,400 and by the plaintiff in the amount of RMB 300. The plaintiff’s litigation fee is waived by this court.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither the plaintiff nor the defendants appealed. The judgment has been executed.
